GENERAL HEADQUARTERS
SUPREME COMMANDER FOR THE ALLIED POWERS
AG 004.01 (17 Oct 46) ESS/IN
(SCAPIN-1278)
APO 500
17 October 1946
MEMORANDUM FOR : THE IMPERIAL JAPANESE GOVERNMENT.
THROUGH : Central Liaison Office, Tokyo.
SUBJECT : Violation of Supreme Commander Allied Powers, Directive No. 1 dated 2 September 1945.
1. Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers Directive No. 1 dated 2 September 1945 required the Japanese Government to hold intact all factories, plants, shops, research institutions, laboratories, testing stations, technical data, etc., intended to produce or to facilitate the production of items intended for use by a military organization.
2. The Imperial Japanese Government is directed to investigate in detail a renorted violation of CAP Directive No. 1. This violation is reported to consist of the transfer of plant equipment, after the effective date of the subject directive, to private ownership and operation of Azuma Kogyo K.K. and later to the Azuma Steel Company of Tokyo.
3. The Imperial Japanese Government will investigate the
disposition of the reported monies paid for these plants by both companies. Written report will be made to the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers within two works after receipt of this memorandum giving full details of this transaction.
4. The Imperial Japanese Government will investigate all similar transactions made subsequent to 2 September 1945 and will submit a full report in this connection within four weeks of receipt of this memorandum.
FOR THE SUPREME COMMANDER:
JOHN B. COOLEY,
Colonel, AGD,
Adjutant General.
